items.title: Hyderabad construction firm alleges 15% commission demands for tenders by Revanth govt
items.summary: A construction company based in Telangana has accused Chief Minister Revanth Reddy’s office of serious irregularities in inviting and evaluating tenders for the Hyderabad Growth Corridor Limited’s (HGCL) Radial Road-2 project. It also alleged that commissions were being demanded for the release of pending payments amounting to over Rs 20,000 crore. The allegations were levelled by RVM Constructions India Limited in a letter to the Builders Association of India (BAI), the apex body of construction companies, seeking their intervention. RVM Constructions managing director Nama Ramesh alleged that the tender process for various projects was manipulated to favour pre-selected bidders. He cited the example of Sushee Infra, which he alleged was disqualified from the bidding process for the Radial Road-2 project using political influence. The letter alleged, “As is widely known, there is a political rift between Shri Rajagopal Reddy and Shri Revanth Reddy.
